subject: Request: carve a short sprint slot for HorizonEdge telemetry export (procurement gating)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: carve a short sprint slot for HorizonEdge telemetry export (procurement gating)

Team —

HorizonEdge is at final procurement review and ProcurementOps has said they need a concrete telemetry/export capability (audit-grade request logs + a simple S3 export for retention) in the POC environment before legal will sign the SOW. They’ve already verbally committed and Anita (cc’d below) said signature is contingent on the timeline.

Why this matters now:
- Deal size: $1.1M ARR first year (expansion potential).
- Procurement window: they need confirmation by EOD Friday (2026-09-10) to keep the commercial cadence.

Asks:
1) Product: can we scope a minimal telemetry export MVP scoped to: request-level logs (json lines), a toggle to enable/disable for the tenant, and a retention export to an S3 bucket?
2) Eng: can we carve a short sprint (2 full dev days + 1 QA day) in the next sprint (starting 2026-09-15) or provide an alternative short-lived workaround (e.g., proxied logging to an existing export pipeline) that satisfies procurement?
3) CS/Sales: if we can commit to a delivery plan, I’ll push for SOW signature and align commercial terms (Ben).

Attachments: telemetry-requirements-HE.xlsx (customer asks), HorizonEdge-SOW-v2.pdf

Irene/Jonas — I know this is tight. Appreciate a rapid take on the minimal acceptable scope and whether an engineering workaround is feasible.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve a short sprint slot for HorizonEdge telemetry export (procurement gating)

Thanks for the context, Tessa. Quick thoughts:

Minimal viable scope we can sign up for (product-side):
- Emit request metadata (timestamp, route, model_id, request_id, tenant_id) to our internal structured logging sink
- Implement an export job that pulls those logs for a given tenant and writes to a customer-provided S3 prefix (with simple CSV/NDJSON format)
- Feature flag at tenant level to opt-in/out (UI toggle not required for MVP; turnkey enable via API or config)
- Retention param in export call (customer manages lifecycle in their S3)

Tradeoffs:
- No immediate PII redaction by default; we'll need HorizonEdge to sign a data-handling attestation (Procurement usually ok with this)
- Observability: we can add minimal metrics for export success/failure, but full telemetry dashboards are out of scope for the 2-day window

If Engineering can provide a quick-priority estimate, we can present a plan to the customer. Jonas — can you confirm if the export job can be implemented as a short-lived runner (leveraging existing export infra) or if it requires a model-serving codepath change?

Irene
Product Manager, Feature Growth

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve a short sprint slot for HorizonEdge telemetry export (procurement gating)

Short answer: feasible as a scoped export job with minimal changes to serving.

Estimate & approach:
- Spike + design: 4 dev hours (get schema + permissions right)
- Implementation: 1.5 engineer-days to wire structured logging out to a tenant-filtered export job that writes NDJSON to S3
- QA + hardening: 1 engineer-day (test tenant, perms, failure modes)
- Hook for a tenant-level toggle: 4–6 hours (API/config)
Total: ~3.5–4.5 engineer-days. If we can accept a very small risk window, we could compress by having an infra-backed export runner use existing logs (reduces dev to ~2.5 engineer-days).

Notes:
- Security: need to ensure S3 write role is least-privilege; we’ll need a short security review (2–4 hours).
- No schema stability guarantee beyond MVP — will version if they want stable contract.

Given the deal pressure, I can try to reprioritize a partial slot for the sprint starting 2026-09-15, but I need product sign-off on the exact fields we ship (Irene).

—Jonas
Sr. Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve a short sprint slot for HorizonEdge telemetry export (procurement gating)

Thanks all — quick commercial context:
- HorizonEdge has indicated they will sign the SOW if we confirm a delivery plan that lands within two weeks of the sprint (i.e., production-ready export within 3 weeks).
- They’ve asked for a small implementation acceptance test (upload + verification) before legal signs.
- I’m authorized to offer a 10% onboarding credit if we can meet the timeline; that helps close the commercial gap.

Proposal to accelerate:
1) Accept the infra-backed export runner approach (low dev cost) as the delivery for procurement sign-off.
2) We commit to a post-MVP follow-up to add schema guarantees & optional redaction.

Tessa — if product+eng can confirm the 2.5–4.5 day window and security review timeline, I’ll get ProcurementOps to mark the SOW as contingent-approved and push legal to finish signatures.

Ben
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Anita Rao <anita@horizonedge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@horizonedge.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve a short sprint slot for HorizonEdge telemetry export (procurement gating)

Tessa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Procurement reviewed the proposed minimal scope and the SOW has been updated to reference the export acceptance test (see attached SOW v2). If Redwood can confirm a technical contact and a short delivery window (we need production export within three calendar weeks), Procurement will proceed to sign.

We can accept the infra-runner approach for now; we will work with your security contact to provision an S3 bucket and an IAM role. Please let us know the contact for the security review.

—Anita Rao
Head of Platform Engineering | HorizonEdge
